headline: Nvidia-led 6.7% Nasdaq-100 rebound on 23 Nov; headlines show a premarket fade

what_happened.summary: Per the Cboe Daily Take 'The Market Taketh and the Market Giveth Back' (23 Nov), Nvidia's announcement that Jensen Huang was back as CEO set off a broad rally. Nvidia closed nearly 31.5% higher, its best day since 2003, and the Nasdaq 100 gained 6.7%, the Nasdaq Composite 6.5%, the S&P 500 4.7% (to 7,237) and the Dow 3%. The S&P 500 and Dow are out of correction territory, while the Nasdaq Composite is still about 13% below its October peak. The Cboe Macro Volatility Digest (week of 23 Nov) says Friday's VIX jump was driven by spot selling and higher fixed-strike vols rather than downside-put demand, and that QQQ 1M implied vol jumped over 20 pts last week. This morning's headlines (unverified) describe Nasdaq futures fading after the Nvidia rally, with Nvidia down in premarket. The inputs contain no live prices, so this brief does not say where NQ trades.
what_happened.market_action: Cboe volatility fell sharply on 23 Nov: VIX 26.62 (-25.83%), VXN 36.31 (-19.76%), VVIX 117.36 (-14.98%), VIX9D 27.76 (-31.83%) and COR1M 25.68 (-28.77%). SKEW rose 1.10% to 140.37. The FRED index series lag and end at 19 Nov (Nasdaq-100 26517.05) and 20 Nov (S&P 500 6910.39), so the 23 Nov index figures come from the Cboe post. Cboe says a rebound does not necessarily end the correction and may be only a reset. Headlines from Kitco, Moomoo, CNBC and Barchart (unverified) describe futures turning lower after the rally; one gives a 1.7% futures decline, and a Yahoo Finance headline gives a 5% Nvidia premarket fall.
what_happened.macro: Treasury (official) 23 Nov: 2-year 4.63% (+0.0 bp), 10-year 4.92% (+0.0 bp), 30-year 5.29% (-2.0 bp), 3-month 4.37% (+5.0 bp), so yields did not rebound with equities. FRED 10y breakeven was 2.13% on 23 Nov and the 10y real yield 2.77% on 20 Nov. HY OAS was 3.76 on 20 Nov (+24.0 bp), the widest in the table and not yet updated for the rally. Polymarket (not CME FedWatch) prices a 25 bp hike in December at 93.5% and 50+ bp at 3.3%. BLS October data: CPI +0.35% m/m, core CPI +0.3%, unemployment 4.1%, payrolls +165.0k.
what_happened.geopolitics: Not covered by the official sources. The Cboe Daily Take of 20 Nov says Middle East conflicts are unresolved. Unverified headlines mention new Iran sanctions and Hormuz (Benzinga) and oil at three-month lows with WTI below $80 (EnergyNow). Another headline says oil rebounded on shipping risks (WSJ). The official oil series (FRED) ends 17 Nov (WTI 89.53, Brent 92.94), so the headline figures cannot be verified.
what_happened.company_news: NVDA 8-K (SEC filing, primary source): the board reinstated Jen-Hsun Huang as President, CEO and director on 22 Nov, effective immediately, and Ms. Kress remains CFO. Cboe says Nvidia options volume ran at roughly three times normal and that Anthropic options already price a $19 implied move to the 18 Dec expiration. CrowdStrike fell nearly 9% and Zscaler rose nearly 18% on the $43.9 billion all-stock deal (Cboe). A META 8-K (primary source) says it will not issue Class C shares while the recapitalization litigation is pending. A Yahoo Finance headline (unverified) cites Goldman Sachs on lingering uncertainty after Huang's return.

driver_reason: Cboe attributes the 23 Nov rally to one Nvidia headline (Huang's return, confirmed by the 8-K) and says sentiment trumped fundamentals. The AI complex, not macro data or rates, is setting the direction of index and volatility moves.
leader_reason: Per Cboe, the Nasdaq 100 rose 6.7% against 4.7% for the S&P 500 on 23 Nov, and VXN minus VIX is 9.69 pts (F44), so tech carries the extra risk premium. The FRED-based Nasdaq-100 minus S&P 500 gap (-0.19 pts last session, -0.78 over 5 sessions) is stale to 19 Nov and predates the rebound. COR1M fell to 25.68 from 36.05, which fits the Digest's picture of an AI-specific rotation rather than a broad macro move.

overlap_with_previous.echo_check: The Nvidia/Huang theme is not an echo today because the 8-K and the 31.5% move are new evidence. The Fed-hike theme is an echo: Polymarket odds are largely unchanged and there is no new official Fed evidence. The premarket-fade story rests only on headlines, which repeat each other, and is not independent confirmation.
